financing.summary: CastleRock Communities LLC is a second-tier subsidiary of Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd. (Tokyo: 1925): Daiwa House USA Holdings Inc. bought 80.0% from the three founders in September 2021 for about US$402 million and, since a 1 December 2025 reorganisation, holds 89.11% of a new Delaware holding company, CRC Holdings LLC, which Daiwa says was set up to facilitate financing for CastleRock; CEO Robert L. (Lance) Wright holds 9.01% and land head Kirk Breitenwischer 1.88%. CastleRock files nothing publicly, so its own bank lines, lot count and any lot-option or land-bank arrangements are not disclosed, and no land banker is named in any source opened in this run. Before Daiwa, the business ran on US$155 million of partner subordinated loans (converted to equity in 2021); today growth is funded by parent equity (CRC Holdings capital stock US$528.6 million) and the parent's yen balance sheet (R&I AA-, JCR AA, funding cost in Japan about 1.3% to 1.4%). Daiwa's three US builders together held 75,017 lots including controlled lots at the end of 2025, about 9.6 years of their combined 7,776 deliveries, and Daiwa does not say how much of that is owned. The opening for a land banker is at parent level: Daiwa's interest-bearing liabilities rose to JPY 3,717.7 billion at 30 September 2026 (debt-equity 1.25x against a former discipline target of about 0.6x), largely from buying real estate for sale including US single-family land, and management said in November 2026 it is considering reducing leverage rather than adding to it.
financing.land_strategy: Not stated in owned-versus-optioned terms. Daiwa describes CastleRock as doing both residential land development and home sales (it self-develops and also sells residential land), and the company's own leadership page says its land head buys both raw land for development and existing (finished) lots. Daiwa's group framing for the US single-family business is growth through M&A plus strategic land acquisition; it reports group land holdings 'including controlled lots' (75,017 at end of 2025) without an owned/controlled split, and publishes no land-light target. Trade press (The Builder's Daily, July 2026) reports a Daiwa aim of about 100,000 controlled US lots under its next plan; that target was not found in Daiwa's own documents opened here. Group tone is land-heavy: Stanley Martin's Steve Alloy, executive chairman of Daiwa House USA Holdings, told the same publication in November 2025 that the industry's land-light model does not fit how his company operates. No equivalent statement from CastleRock was found.

lots.source_title: Daiwa House: FY2025 Presentation on Management Policies (18 May 2026), page 7
lots.note: CastleRock's own lot count, owned/optioned split and years of supply are not publicly disclosed, so the fields are blank. The only public number is for Daiwa's three US builders combined (Stanley Martin, Trumark, CastleRock): total land holdings of 75,017 lots including controlled lots at the end of December 2025, up 47% from 50,933 at the end of December 2021. Against 7,776 combined deliveries in FY2025 that is roughly 9.6 years of supply for the group (own arithmetic, not a company figure). Daiwa does not split the 75,017 between owned and controlled or by builder. CastleRock scale markers: 1,465 homes delivered and US$645 million net sales in the latest year reported for it, 268 employees at end of December 2024.

land_banking.counterparty: Daiwa House USA Holdings Inc. (parent; wholly owned by Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.)
land_banking.description: Not a land banker or lot-option program: this is the parent equity owner. Daiwa House USA Holdings holds 89.11% of CRC Holdings LLC, the holding company set up on 1 December 2025 to facilitate financing for CastleRock Communities LLC (capital stock US$528.608 million). Four Daiwa officers or employees also serve as officers of CRC Holdings and Daiwa staff are seconded to it.
land_banking.source_title: Daiwa House: Notice Concerning Change of Specified Subsidiary in the United States
land_banking.note: Amount left blank because US$528.6 million is the holding company's capital stock, not a facility size. No third-party land banker or lot-option financier is named for CastleRock in any source opened. 2026-11-19 check: description previously said this equity funds CastleRock land; the source says only that the holding company was set up to facilitate financing, so that wording was removed.

At that date CastleRock had total assets of US$271.9 million and net assets of US$41.3 million, so other liabilities (bank debt and payables, not broken out) were roughly US$75 million.

Up from JPY 3,076.7 billion at 31 March 2026. Debt-equity 1.25x (1.16x after 50% equity credit on JPY 250 billion of hybrids). Roughly US$23.7 billion at JPY 156.56 per dollar (the rate Daiwa itself used for December 2025; indicative only).

capital_events.description: Holding-company reorganisation: CRC Holdings LLC (Delaware) was set up above CastleRock Communities LLC, stated purpose to facilitate financing for CastleRock. Existing holders swapped their CastleRock interests for CRC Holdings interests. Capital stock US$528.608 million; holders Daiwa House USA Holdings 89.11%, Robert L. Wright 9.01%, Kirk T. Breitenwischer 1.88%.
capital_events.source_title: Daiwa House: Notice Concerning Change of Specified Subsidiary in the United States
capital_events.note: Approved by the subsidiary's board 21 October 2025, effective 1 December 2025, announced 20 February 2026. What financing the new structure is meant to carry (bank facility, notes, parent loans) is not disclosed. Inference: capital stock of US$528.6 million against a 2021 investment amount of about US$158 million suggests large capital contributions since the acquisition, but the two figures may not be measured the same way. Ownership change visible here (moved from a removed M&A row, 2026-11-19): Daiwa bought 80.0% in 2021 (release 2021-08-10) and holds 89.11% after the reorganisation; co-founder Gregory A. Yakim, a 2021 seller, is no longer a holder. When and how the stake rose (purchase of Yakim interest, capital injections, or both) is not disclosed.

capital_events.description: Parent half-year results: interest-bearing liabilities (excluding leases) rose to JPY 3,717.7 billion from JPY 3,076.7 billion in six months, funded by bank borrowings and commercial paper, mainly to buy real estate for sale in the single-family and commercial businesses; debt-equity 1.25x. On the results call management said it is considering reducing interest-bearing liabilities going forward. The US single-family delivery forecast for the year was raised from 8,000 to 9,000 homes, about 1,500 of them from acquired companies.
capital_events.source_title: Daiwa House: Q&A at Earnings Conference for FY2026 2Q (Summary)
capital_events.note: Parent-level. Balance-sheet figures are from the earnings release of the same date (https://www.daiwahouse.com/English/ir/financial_results/pdf/DaiwaHouseFResultFY2026_2Q.pdf). Management also said the US single-family market shows no sign of recovery and incentives stay high.

capital_events.description: Trade press reports Daiwa House aims for about 100,000 controlled US lots (from just over 75,000) and about 10,000 US single-family deliveries a year, and may make more acquisitions under its next medium-term plan; its US builders are described as funded with the parent's patient capital, with no financing terms given.
capital_events.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: The Holiday acquisition is about Daiwa House's next decade
capital_events.note: Group-level, not CastleRock-specific. The article does not say whether the lots are owned or optioned and does not mention land banking.

key_metrics.credit_ratings: CastleRock itself: no public rating. Parent Daiwa House Industry long-term issuer ratings: R&I AA-, JCR AA.
key_metrics.source_title: Daiwa House Group: Ratings (investor relations page)

ma.description: CastleRock, through its wholly owned CastleRock Communities Alabama, LLC, bought the single-family business of WrEn Homes: its land and buildings plus the construction and sales staff. WrEn delivered 80 homes and had US$47 million of sales in FY2024, with 14 employees; it sells mainly to move-up buyers. Price not disclosed.
ma.map_impact: Adds Alabama (Huntsville) as CastleRock's fourth state after Texas, Arizona (organic, July 2023) and Tennessee (The Jones Company of Tennessee, January 2024). Brings in WrEn's local leaders (founders Jim Wright and Jeff Enfinger, president Caleb McWhorter at signing) and a small owned land position; adds roughly 80 closings a year.
ma.source_title: Daiwa House: First Entry into Alabama, U.S. CastleRock Communities LLC Acquires WrEn's Single-Family Housing Business
ma.note: Closed 31 October 2025 US time (1 November in Japan); announced 4 November 2025. Whether the WrEn principals stayed on after closing is not stated.

gaps: Lots owned, lots optioned, total controlled and years of supply for CastleRock: not publicly disclosed. Daiwa House gives only a combined figure for its three US builders (75,017 lots including controlled lots at end of December 2025) with no split by builder or by owned versus controlled.
Land-banking or lot-option counterparties: none named in any source read. Not confirmed absent: press was checked only through direct pages.
Any link to Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose Properties, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon: none found in the sources opened.
CastleRock-level credit facilities (revolver, term loans, agent bank, lenders, size, maturity): not publicly disclosed.
Whether CastleRock borrows from US banks, from Daiwa House USA Holdings or from the parent, and what financing CRC Holdings LLC was created to carry: not publicly disclosed.
CastleRock cash, debt, liquidity and leverage: not publicly disclosed. Last public balance sheet is 31 December 2020 (total assets US$271.9 million, net assets US$41.3 million).
WrEn Homes purchase price and lots acquired: not publicly disclosed.
CastleRock's 2026 year-to-date sales and deliveries: not retrieved (they sit in Daiwa House 'Financial Highlights' and Factbook PDFs, which were not read).

Reporting-year conflict: Daiwa's November 2025 release labels 1,465 deliveries and US$645 million sales as FY2024, while its Integrated Report 2026 shows 1,465 as CastleRock's FY2025 deliveries (the three US builders sum to the FY2025 total of 7,776). Treat the year attached to 1,465 as unsettled.
Parent zero coupon convertible bonds due 2029 and 2030: principal amounts not in the document opened.

M&A after May 2026: no CastleRock deal found. Sister-company deals (Stanley Martin: United Homes Group, May 2026, and Holiday Builders, July 2026; Trumark: JK Monarch, March 2026) belong on those builders' records.

Daiwa group stance on third-party land banking: no statement found. The only signals are indirect (parent leverage above target; a reported 100,000 controlled-lot aim; Stanley Martin's leader rejecting land-light for his own company).

Daiwa stake increase from 80.0% (2021) to 89.11% (December 2025) and the exit of co-founder Gregory A. Yakim: no transaction date, price or mechanism disclosed. The December 2025 CRC Holdings reorganisation itself was an internal share exchange, so it is recorded under capital_events, not M&A (M&A row removed in the 2026-11-19 check).
